chapter: Ellington, singers, the book and closing
title: Ella Fitzgerald and Ray Brown; singing without soul
summary: Mingus attacks Ella as cruel and soulless and says Ben Webster beat her; he prefers Dinah Washington.

venues.name: Chamber Music Society of Lower Basin Street

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them

blocks.x: Yeah. It somehow reminds me of his former wife, Ella.
Oh, man, Jesus Christ.
Because I never thought she knew what she was singing, or cared.

She talked to him like a dog, man. She's evil. She led him on. But I remember this bass player, Jack Lander, (unintelligible) in Canada, told me Ray -- I never really knew him that well. We were talking about bass, -- hey, you. Hey, you.
Yeah.
You hear me? Come here. He was very cool. He said, (inaudible). So I knew that wouldn't last.
Yeah.
I guess some guys will do anything for money.
But it sounds corny, but --
Ben Webster beat the shit out of her.
Who did?
Ben Webster.
Really?
He (inaudible) take care of that bitch.
Well, why would he get angry with her? Because of what she'd say to him?
She was cruel, man. She was like a man.
Yeah. But, you know, that old --
Hey, man, you know, a lot of people who are famous ain't that famous. They think they're better than somebody else.
Yeah.
And she's one of them. I don't know about now, but she was then.
Yeah. But it's interesting, Charlie Parker used to say, whoever you are comes through what you do musically.
Yeah, well, Bird was sweet, Duke was sweet.
And she was -- there was no soul in her singing.
I never appreciated it at all.
No. So that really -- that makes sense, the kind of life you live and what your values are comes out in the music. You never recorded with her, did you?
(Inaudible.) Recorded with Dinah Shore, Dinah Washington. Who has more soul than she had?
She did. She used to do a radio show,
years ago, the Chamber Music Society of Lower Basin Street. She wasn't bad. You still interested -- I remember, we used to talk a lot --
